description: Data-calibrated Financial Health Score (python main.py calibrate). Each ratio's breakpoints are percentiles (P5-P95) of a reference universe (NIFTY 500 + S&P 500, non-financial companies), computed within the company's sector when the sector has enough observations, so points approximate the company's percentile rank among its peers (Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen 2019). Ratio weights WITHIN each category are CRITIC objective weights (Diakoulaki et al. 1995). Category weights come from a supervised logistic regression of a next-year distress proxy (net loss or negative operating cash flow) on the five category scores: weight = max(0, -coefficient on the raw score scale), normalised to sum to 1, used because it passed a pre-declared acceptance rule (out-of-fold AUC above every simple composite by >= 0.02, AUC CI above 0.5, no significantly wrong-signed coefficient). A category whose coefficient is not negative (e.g. liquidity) receives weight 0: it is still shown, graded and checked by red flags but does not move the overall score. Interpretation bands are the universe quartiles of the overall score, so labels describe relative position among large listed companies. Missing data never receives points; it lowers data coverage. Academic indicator only - not a credit rating or investment advice. Full evidence: docs/calibration/CALIBRATION_REPORT.md and docs/SCORING_METHODOLOGY.md
sector_exclusions_note: Categories listed for a sector are NOT APPLICABLE to it and are not scored (they do not lower data coverage). Banks/insurers: working-capital liquidity, asset turnover and operating cash flow (which includes deposit and loan flows) do not measure their health; bank-specific metrics are outside the Semester 1 scope, so their overall score is unavailable rather than misleading.

calibration.category_weight_note: Weights in this file (v2.1.0) were normalised from STANDARDISED logistic coefficients and applied to raw 0-100 category scores. The calibrator now divides by each score's standard deviation first (beta / sd). Because the five category scores have similar spreads (sd 22-26), the corrected weights differ by at most ~0.02 per category; re-running 'python main.py calibrate --apply' would adopt them. See docs/SCORING_METHODOLOGY.md, section 'Known calibration issue'.

grade_bands_note: Letter grades follow Morningstar's documented Financial Health grade distribution (top 10% A, next 20% B, middle 40% C, next 20% D, bottom 10% F); cut-offs are the universe P90/P70/P30/P10 of each category score.
